Three different "yields" get quoted for $SCHD $JEPI $JEPQ $QQQI $VOO: 
 
• Trailing (TTM) yield: what was actually paid over the last 12 months ÷ price 
• Distribution rate: the latest payout annualised ÷ price (can swing month to month) 
• 30-day SEC yield: a standardised, net-of-expenses measure that leaves out option premiums, so covered-call funds can look very different on it 
 
Same fund, three numbers. Compare like with like.

On Stocktwits, bullish tags (8) slightly outnumber bearish ones (6), so sentiment is cautiously optimistic but far from euphoric. Another thread digs into memory chip shortages, with Dell's CEO warning that DRAM supply will get worse before it gets better, and traders debating whether that's bullish for chip names like Micron and Western Digital. There's also a fair amount of noise: jokes about overtrading, political jabs tied to DJT and the White House, and complaints about copy-trading accounts. For regular investors, the key takeaway is that QQQ discussion is being driven by macro fear and AI enthusiasm in roughly equal measure. The sharp drop in Reddit mentions could mean retail attention is thinning, which historically can precede quieter, trend-following moves rather than wild swings. But the Stocktwits crowd is still actively positioning, and the AI supply-chain debate is a real fundamental thread worth following. Watch Nvidia earnings, memory pricing, and any White House policy headlines, because those are the things this community is actually trading around.

DTE.summary: DTE Energy is getting a surprising amount of attention for a regulated utility, with Reddit mentions at 38 over the past 24 hours, down from 63 the day before, ranking it 8th overall. On Stocktwits, bullish tags outnumber bearish ones 15 to 1, and the message board is filled with retail investors who seem to view this as a safe, income-generating play. The most concrete catalyst is news that Michigan regulators approved DTE's 20-year power contracts for Google's 1-gigawatt data center near Detroit, known as Project Cannoli. The deal includes ratepayer protections, with Google paying a minimum billing demand of 80 percent of contracted capacity even if it doesn't use all the power. That's a big deal because it ties a stable utility to the AI data center boom, giving DTE a growth angle beyond its traditional regulated business. Users are posting things like 'this should never be down, they have a monopoly on all electricity' and 'seems like a no brainer here.' One user mentioned buying 2,400 shares and expects the stock to hit $140 soon, plus a dividend coming on the 15th. Another noted that energy stocks across the board were green, including Vistra, Constellation, AEP, and Duke, suggesting sector-wide strength. There's also mention of Peter Thiel's promising energy portfolio, which includes DTE alongside Amazon, Vistra, CMS, and AEP. The tone is overwhelmingly positive, with people buying a few shares a day and expressing confidence in the dividend and growth prospects. Investors should know that DTE is being viewed as a way to play both the AI power demand theme and the defensive utility sector. The Google data center contract provides a visible long-term revenue stream, and the dividend adds appeal for income-focused investors. However, utilities are still subject to regulatory risks, and the stock's recent popularity might be partly due to sector rotation rather than company-specific fundamentals. The low bearish sentiment suggests little concern among retail, but that could change if interest rates rise or regulatory decisions turn unfavorable.

AGI.summary: The online discussion around AGI is a bit of a mess right now because the ticker is being used for two completely different things. On one hand, there's a gold and silver mining company called Alamos Gold that trades under AGI, and on the other hand, there's a tiny cryptocurrency memecoin also called AGI, which stands for 'Artificial Gato Intelligence' (a cat-themed joke). This confusion is driving a lot of the chatter, and it's important for investors to know which one they're actually looking at. The Reddit mentions dropped from 29 to 23 in the last 24 hours, but it still ranks 11th, so there's decent interest. On Stocktwits, the sentiment is overwhelmingly bullish with 14 bullish tags and zero bearish tags, but that's likely skewed by the memecoin crowd. Looking at the messages, some are clearly about the gold stock: one user says 'never hurts to own some gold and silver.. physical and mkt' and another mentions 'saw this vid. wt called gold and silver. i'm still holding strong.' There's also a message about options activity on AGI, mentioning December $45 calls with over 10,200 contracts swept at the ask, which is about $1.63M in premium, and another about October $31 calls with 36k contracts. These are likely referring to Alamos Gold, which trades around $30-40. But then there are multiple messages pumping the AGI memecoin, calling it 'the only memecoin below 100K mc that can run 100 to 1000X' and describing its features like a launchpad for tokenized stocks, cross-chain swap bridge, telegram bot, and a social trading platform. One user even says 'the best memecoin under 50K market cap on $HOOD chain is $AGI' and calls it a 'cat memecoin with utility.' This is classic memecoin shilling, and it's creating noise. Investors should be aware that the bullish tags on Stocktwits might be from memecoin enthusiasts, not from serious gold investors. The gold stock itself is a real company with fundamentals, and the options activity suggests some big players are betting on upside, but the stock is down about 5% today according to one message. The memecoin is extremely risky and speculative, with a market cap under 100K, so it could be a scam or a pump-and-dump. The key takeaway is to verify which AGI you're trading. If you're interested in the gold miner, look at its financials, production, and gold prices. If you're looking at the memecoin, be prepared to lose everything. The community discussion is fragmented, and the bullish sentiment is not uniform. Overall, there's excitement about potential big moves in both, but the lack of bearish tags on Stocktwits is suspicious and might indicate a echo chamber. Investors should do their own research and not rely on memecoin hype.

V.summary: Visa (ticker V) isn't getting much love on Reddit right now—zero mentions in the last 24 hours, same as the day before—but over on Stocktwits, the conversation is alive and mostly bullish. The sentiment tags show 15 bullish versus just 2 bearish, and the messages paint a picture of traders who see Visa as a quiet winner in a messy macro environment. One popular post (14 likes) points out the irony that crypto and AI were supposed to disrupt Visa and Mastercard, yet both are hitting all-time highs. The argument is that more inflation leads to more nominal spending, which means more transaction fees for Visa, while the credit risk stays with the banks. That's a classic 'toll booth' thesis: Visa doesn't lend money, it just takes a cut of every swipe. Another user is dreaming about a big options move—calls at the $430 strike with over $8 million in open interest, which would imply an 8% jump. That's speculative, but it shows some traders are betting on upside. There's also a note that Visa has rallied 35% since April 1 with no change in earnings, pushing its valuation to 30 times current earnings and 32 times trailing. That's rich for a company growing earnings in the low-to-mid teens, and one poster flags it as 'pretty far askew.' Still, others see 'massive breakouts' in Visa and Mastercard, and some are even calling for another stock split (Visa last split in 2015). A few messages are just ticker spam or unrelated hype, but the overall tone is positive. Investors should know that Visa's business is fundamentally strong—it benefits from inflation, digital payments growth, and a wide moat—but the stock isn't cheap. The bull case rests on resilient consumer spending and fee-based revenue; the bear case is that valuation leaves little room for error, especially if spending slows. With no Reddit buzz, this is more of an institutional and options-trader story right now. Keep an eye on consumer spending data and any regulatory noise around swipe fees, but for now, the Stocktwits crowd is leaning bullish.
